Serve with red cabbage, avocado slices, coriander and lime.

title: Ghormeh Sabzi – Persian Herb Stew with Beef, Kidney Beans and Rice
ingredients: Dried lime, turmeric, fenugreek leaves, salt
instructions: Dice the onion and fry in half of the oil until golden brown. Add the beef and turmeric and brown all over.
Pour in 400 ml water, add the pierced dried lime and braise, covered, for 50 minutes.
Finely chop the herbs, leek greens and spinach and sweat in the remaining oil with the fenugreek for 8 minutes until dark green.
Add the herbs and kidney beans to the meat and simmer for another 20 minutes.
Cook the basmati rice and serve with the stew.

title: Jerusalem Artichoke and Parsnip Soup with Hazelnuts and Wholegrain Bread
instructions: Scrub the Jerusalem artichokes thoroughly, peel the parsnip and roughly dice both with the onion.
Sweat the vegetables in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes, pour in the stock and simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Add the oat drink and blend everything until smooth. Season with nutmeg, marjoram, salt and pepper.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan and roughly chop.
Sprinkle the soup with the hazelnuts and serve with the wholegrain bread. Drink plenty of fluids with it.

title: Nasu Dengaku – Miso Aubergine with Edamame and Brown Rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice its volume of water for 30–35 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Halve the aubergine lengthways, score the flesh in a diamond pattern, brush with rapeseed oil and bake cut side up for 20 minutes.
Stir the miso with the maple syrup, sesame oil and 1 tbsp water until smooth, spread over the aubergines and caramelise under the grill for 4 minutes.
Cook the edamame in salted water for 4 minutes.
Sprinkle the aubergines with sesame seeds and spring onions and serve with the rice and edamame.

title: Beef Bulgogi with Barley Rice, Spinach Namul and Kimchi
instructions: Mix the beef with soy sauce, grated pear and garlic and marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Rinse the rice and pearl barley together and cook with 200 ml water for 25 minutes (bori-bap).
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately for 1 minute each, squeeze out and dress with sesame oil, sesame seeds and salt. Cut the carrot into strips.
Sear the meat in a very hot pan for 2–3 minutes.
Serve the barley rice with the bulgogi, namul, carrot and kimchi.

title: Aloo Gobi with Peas and Wholemeal Chapati
ingredients: Cumin, turmeric, garam masala, coriander, salt
instructions: Knead the wholemeal flour with a pinch of salt and about 30 ml water into a smooth dough and leave to rest for 15 minutes.
Toast the cumin in the rapeseed oil, add the onion and ginger and fry for 4 minutes. Stir in the tomato and turmeric.
Add the cauliflower florets and diced potato and cook, covered, with 80 ml water for 15 minutes. Add the peas and garam masala and cook uncovered for another 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into two pieces, roll out thinly and cook in a hot dry pan for 1 minute per side until it blisters.
Sprinkle the aloo gobi with coriander and serve with the chapatis.

title: Hake on Bean and Fennel Ragout
instructions: Cut the fennel into thin strips, dice the tomatoes and chop the garlic.
Sweat the fennel and garlic in half of the olive oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes, paprika, saffron and stock and simmer for 8 minutes.
Fold in the beans, warm for 3 minutes and season with salt.
Salt the hake and fry in the remaining oil for 3 minutes per side.
Divide the ragout between deep plates, place the fish on top and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Pan-Fried Mackerel with Barley, Kale and Pear Salad
instructions: Cook the pearl barley in three times its volume of salted water for 25 minutes and drain.
Cut the kale into thin strips and massage with a pinch of salt by hand for 1 minute until soft.
Stir together the mustard, vinegar and rapeseed oil. Cut the pear into wedges and the onion into thin rings and mix with the barley, kale and dressing.
Fry the mackerel skin side down in a hot dry pan for 4 minutes until crisp, turn and finish cooking for 1 minute.
Sprinkle the salad with toasted walnuts and place the mackerel on top.

title: Prawn and Okra Gumbo with Brown Rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice its volume of water for 30–35 minutes.
Toast the rapeseed oil and flour in a pot for 8–10 minutes, stirring constantly, into a hazelnut-brown roux.
Dice the onion, pepper and celery, add and sweat for 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, stock, Cajun seasoning, thyme and bay leaf.
Slice the okra, add and simmer for 20 minutes until the gumbo has thickened.
Poach the prawns in it for the last 4 minutes. Serve with the rice.

title: Turkey Breast with Wild Rice, Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Lingonberries
instructions: Cook the wild rice in plenty of salted water for 40 minutes and drain.
Preheat the oven to 210°C. Halve the Brussels sprouts, cut the onion into wedges, toss with half of the oil, salt and pepper and roast for 25 minutes.
Season the turkey breast with sage, thyme, salt and pepper and fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes per side, then leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Roughly chop and briefly toast the pecans and fold into the wild rice with the Brussels sprouts.
Slice the turkey, arrange on the wild rice and serve with lingonberries.

title: Freekeh with Chicken, Chickpeas and Almonds
instructions: Dice the onion and fry in half of the olive oil until golden brown. Add the freekeh and baharat and toast for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and 100 ml water and cook, covered, for 20 minutes. Fold in the chickpeas for the last 5 minutes.
Season the chicken breast with baharat, cinnamon and salt and fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes per side, rest briefly and cut into strips.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden brown.
Serve the freekeh with the chicken, sprinkle with almonds and parsley and serve with yoghurt.

title: Lupin Patties with Red Cabbage and Apple Salad and Potatoes
ingredients: Parsley, marjoram, cider vinegar, salt, pepper
instructions: Pour 80 ml hot water over the lupin grits and leave to swell for 10 minutes. Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20 minutes.
Finely shred the red cabbage and briefly knead with salt; cut the apple into matchsticks and mix with the cider vinegar and 1 tsp oil.
Finely dice the onion and knead with the lupin grits, oats, mustard, marjoram, parsley, salt and pepper. Shape four flat patties.
Fry the patties in the remaining rapeseed oil for 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve with the red cabbage and apple salad and the potatoes.

title: Wholewheat Orecchiette with Broccoli, Anchovies and Chilli
instructions: Divide the broccoli into small florets; peel and dice the stalk.
Cook the orecchiette in plenty of salted water, adding the broccoli halfway through the cooking time, and cook everything together until al dente.
Heat the olive oil with the garlic, anchovies and chilli until the anchovies break down.
Add the pasta and broccoli to the pan with a little cooking water and toss until the broccoli partly breaks down and forms a sauce.
Serve with lemon zest and Parmesan.

title: Red-Red – Ghanaian Black-Eyed Bean Stew with Baked Plantain
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Peel the plantain, slice diagonally, brush with 1 tsp oil and bake for 20 minutes until golden brown, turning once.
Dice the onion and fry in the remaining oil with ginger, chilli and paprika for 5 minutes.
Briefly toast the tomato purée, dice the tomatoes, add and reduce for 10 minutes into a thick red sauce.
Fold in the beans, simmer for 8 minutes and season with salt.
Serve the beans with the baked plantain.

title: Sichuan Green Beans with Pork Fillet, Shiitake and Brown Rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice its volume of water for 30–35 minutes.
Cut the pork fillet into thin strips and marinate in half of the soy sauce. Slice the shiitake.
Trim the beans and stir-fry in a hot wok with half of the oil for 6–8 minutes until the skin blisters. Remove.
Heat the remaining oil, sear the meat for 2 minutes, add the shiitake, garlic, ginger, chillies and Sichuan pepper and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and remaining soy sauce, toss briefly and serve with the rice.

title: Babgulyás – Hungarian Bean Goulash Soup with Beef
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the rapeseed oil until golden. Cut the beef into small cubes, add and brown all over.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika, caraway and tomato purée, then pour in the stock and simmer, covered, for 40 minutes.
Dice the carrot, parsnip, potato and pepper, add and cook for another 20 minutes.
Add the beans and cook for 5 minutes. Season with marjoram and salt.
Serve in deep plates or soup bowls.

title: Çılbır – Poached Eggs on Garlic Yoghurt with Spinach Bulgur
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the olive oil, stir in the tomato purée and bulgur, pour in 150 ml water and leave to swell, covered, for 12 minutes.
Roughly chop the spinach and fold into the bulgur until wilted. Season with salt.
Stir the yoghurt with grated garlic and a pinch of salt and spread on a plate.
Poach the eggs in simmering vinegar water for 3–4 minutes and place on the yoghurt.
Foam the butter with pul biber (Aleppo pepper flakes), drizzle over the eggs, sprinkle with dill and serve with the spinach bulgur.

title: Gigantes Plaki – Greek Baked Giant Beans with Feta
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Finely dice the onion, carrot, celery and garlic and sweat in the olive oil for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 5 minutes. Fold in the beans and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer everything to a small baking dish and bake for 30 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the beans on top are lightly toasted.
Crumble the feta over, sprinkle with dill and serve with the bread.

title: Fattoush with Chickpeas and Toasted Wholemeal Pitta
instructions: Tear the pitta into bite-sized pieces and toast in the oven at 200°C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Rinse the chickpeas, pat dry and toast with sumac in a dry pan for 5 minutes.
Roughly chop the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes and pepper and pick the herb leaves.
Stir the olive oil with lemon juice, sumac and salt and toss with the vegetables, chickpeas and herbs.
Just before serving, fold in the pitta chips and sprinkle with pomegranate seeds.

title: Santorini Fava with Grilled Squid and Capers
instructions: Wash the split peas thoroughly and bring to the boil with the onion, garlic and stock. Skim and simmer, covered, for 40 minutes until very soft.
Blend until smooth with half of the olive oil, the lemon juice and salt.
Clean the inside of the squid, score in a diamond pattern, season with oregano and salt and grill in a very hot griddle pan with a little oil for 1–2 minutes per side.
Spread the fava on plates, place the squid on top and finish with capers, red onion rings and the remaining oil.
Serve with tomato wedges and lemon.

title: Massaman Curry with Tofu, Squash and Peanuts
ingredients: Massaman curry paste (vegan, no shrimp paste)
instructions: Cook the jasmine rice according to the packet instructions. Dice the tofu and fry in a dry non-stick pan until golden brown all over.
Toast the curry paste in a pot with 2 tbsp coconut milk until fragrant.
Dice the squash, potatoes and onion, add, pour in the remaining coconut milk and 150 ml water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the pepper, tofu and spinach and cook for 5 minutes. Season with tamarind, lime and soy sauce.
Sprinkle with toasted peanuts and serve with the rice.

title: Lamb Fillet with Pea and Mint Purée, Rosemary Potatoes and Carrots
ingredients: Fresh mint, rosemary, lemon, salt, pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C. Quarter the potatoes, toss with half of the oil, rosemary and salt and roast for 25 minutes. Add the carrot batons after 10 minutes.
Cook the peas in a little salted water for 4 minutes, drain and roughly purée with the yoghurt, mint and a squeeze of lemon.
Season the lamb fillet with salt and pepper and fry in the remaining oil for 6–8 minutes all over until pink, then leave to rest for 3 minutes.
Slice the lamb and serve with the pea purée, rosemary potatoes and carrots.

title: Lentil and Mushroom Shepherd's Pie with Sweet Potato Topping
instructions: Wash the sweet potato thoroughly, dice with its skin, cook in salted water for 15 minutes until soft and roughly mash.
Finely dice the onion, carrot and mushrooms and fry vigorously in the rapeseed oil for 6 minutes. Briefly toast the tomato purée.
Add the lentils, stock, soy sauce and herbs and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft and the filling is thick.
Transfer the filling to a baking dish, spread the sweet potato mash on top and draw grooves with a fork.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until the topping is golden brown. Keeps for 3 days in portions in the fridge.

title: Tofu Bánh Mì with Pickled Vegetables and Coriander
instructions: Cut the carrot and radish into fine matchsticks and pickle them with the rice vinegar, maple syrup and a pinch of salt for at least 15 minutes.
Cut the tofu into 1 cm thick slices, pat dry thoroughly and marinate in the soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Fry the tofu in the rapeseed oil for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden brown.
Slice the baguette open lengthways and crisp it up briefly in the oven.
Fill with the tofu, drained vegetables, cucumber strips, chilli rings and coriander, and drizzle with sriracha.

title: Tempeh Balado – Tempeh in Chilli-Tomato Sambal with Rice and Green Beans
instructions: Cook the jasmine rice according to the packet instructions. Trim the green beans and cook in salted water for 6 minutes until al dente.
Cut the tempeh into thin slices and fry in half of the oil for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Roughly blitz the chillies, shallots, garlic and tomatoes into a paste in a blender.
Cook the paste down in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until it is a glossy deep red. Season with the sugar, salt and lime juice.
Add the tempeh to the sambal, toss briefly and serve with the rice and beans.

title: Seitan Stroganoff with Mushrooms and Wholewheat Tagliatelle
instructions: Cook the tagliatelle in salted water according to the packet instructions.
Cut the seitan into thin strips, sear in half of the oil over high heat for 4 minutes and set aside.
Cut the onion into strips and slice the mushrooms, then fry in the remaining oil for 6 minutes. Briefly toast the paprika with them.
Deglaze with the stock, stir in the mustard and reduce for 3 minutes. Lower the heat, stir in the soy yoghurt and seitan and only warm through – do not boil.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with the pasta and parsley.

title: Hong Shao Tofu – Red-Braised Tofu with Shiitake, Pak Choi and Rice
instructions: Cook the rice. Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes, pat dry and fry in the oil until golden brown all over, then set aside.
Sweat the ginger, garlic and the white part of the spring onion in the remaining oil and lightly caramelise the sugar in it.
Add the sliced shiitake, deglaze with the soy sauce, star anise and 120 ml water, and return the tofu to the pan.
Braise covered for 10 minutes, then reduce uncovered until the sauce glazes the tofu.
Halve the pak choi, steam for 2 minutes and arrange with the tofu, rice and spring onion greens.

title: Tofu Tikka Masala with Basmati Rice
ingredients: Garam masala, turmeric, paprika, dried fenugreek leaves, coriander
instructions: Dice the tofu, mix with the soy yoghurt, garam masala, paprika and salt and marinate for 15 minutes.
Roast the tofu on a lined baking tray at 220°C for 15 minutes until the edges darken. Cook the basmati rice.
Finely chop the onion, ginger and garlic and fry in the oil for 6 minutes until golden brown. Briefly toast the turmeric and garam masala with them.
Add the passata and reduce for 10 minutes, then stir in the coconut milk and crumbled fenugreek leaves.
Add the tofu to the sauce, let it infuse for 2 minutes and serve with the rice and coriander.

title: Cuban Picadillo with Soy Mince, Olives, Raisins and Rice
instructions: Pour the hot stock over the soy mince and leave to soak for 10 minutes. Cook the rice.
Finely dice the onion, pepper and garlic and sweat in the olive oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the soaked mince with its liquid and fry for 4 minutes until crumbly. Stir in the cumin and oregano.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaf, halved olives and raisins and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Season with salt and serve with the rice.

title: Lentil Sloppy Joes on Wholegrain Rolls with Coleslaw
instructions: Boil the lentils in plenty of water for 20–25 minutes until tender, then drain.
Finely shred the white cabbage, grate the carrot and knead well with the cider vinegar, salt and a pinch of sugar.
Finely dice the onion and pepper and fry in the oil for 5 minutes. Briefly toast the tomato purée and smoked paprika with them.
Add the lentils, passata, mustard and maple syrup and cook down for 8 minutes into a thick, juicy mixture.
Slice the rolls open, toast them, fill with the lentil mixture and serve with the coleslaw.

title: Pasta e Ceci – Roman Pasta with Chickpeas and Rosemary
instructions: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery and sweat with the garlic and rosemary in half of the olive oil for 6 minutes.
Briefly toast the tomato purée, add the chickpeas and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Purée a third of the chickpeas with a little liquid and return to the pan.
Cook the pasta directly in the soup for 10 minutes, stirring, until al dente and creamy.
Season with salt, pepper and chilli and serve drizzled with the remaining olive oil.

title: Vegan Cassoulet with White Beans, Smoked Tofu and Herb Crumbs
ingredients: Thyme, bay leaf, parsley, salt, pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Dice the smoked tofu and fry in half of the oil for 4 minutes until crisp.
Dice the onion, carrot, celery and garlic and sweat briefly with the tofu.
Add the beans, tomatoes, stock, thyme and bay leaf, season with salt and pepper and transfer everything to a small baking dish.
Mix the panko with chopped parsley and the remaining oil and sprinkle over the top.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and the crumbs are golden brown.

title: Seitan with Mojo Verde and Papas Arrugadas
instructions: Cook the potatoes in their skins in heavily salted water for 20 minutes, drain and let them dry in the pan until a salt crust forms.
For the mojo verde, finely purée the herbs, pepper, garlic, cumin, vinegar and 10 g olive oil with 2 tbsp water.
Slice the seitan and sear in the remaining oil in a griddle pan for 3 minutes per side.
Dice the tomato and cucumber and season with salt.
Arrange the seitan with the potatoes, salad and plenty of mojo verde.

title: Kongguksu – Korean Cold Soy Milk Noodles with Cucumber and Tomato
instructions: Blend the tofu, soy drink and 8 g sesame seeds until very smooth, season with salt and chill for at least 20 minutes.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions, drain and rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Cut the cucumber into fine strips and the tomato into wedges.
Place the noodles in a deep bowl, pour over the ice-cold soy soup and add a few ice cubes.
Top with the cucumber, tomato and remaining sesame seeds.

title: Tofu Katsu Curry with Rice
instructions: Cook the rice. Cut the onion into strips and the carrot and potato into cubes, and sweat in 3 g oil for 5 minutes.
Dust with 8 g flour and the curry powder, toast briefly, deglaze with the stock, add the apple and soy sauce and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Cut the tofu into two flat slices, pat dry and coat first in the remaining flour, then in the soy drink and finally in the panko.
Drizzle the tofu katsu with the remaining oil and bake on baking paper for 18 minutes until golden brown and crisp, turning once.
Slice the katsu into strips and serve with the rice and curry sauce.

title: Tofu Larb with Sticky Rice and Crunchy Raw Vegetables
ingredients: Glutinous rice (uncooked, incl. 10 g for toasted rice powder)
instructions: Soak 50 g glutinous rice for at least 4 hours and steam for 25 minutes.
Toast 10 g glutinous rice in a dry pan until golden brown and grind to a coarse powder in a mortar.
Finely crumble the tofu and fry in the oil for 8 minutes until dry and slightly crisp.
Take the pan off the heat and mix the tofu with the lime juice, soy sauce, chilli, shallot rings, spring onion, herbs and toasted rice powder.
Serve with the sticky rice, cucumber, beans and lettuce leaves for wrapping.

title: Mercimek Köftesi – Red Lentil and Bulgur Patties with Salad and Pomegranate
ingredients: Pul biber (Aleppo pepper), cumin, lemon, salt
instructions: Cook the lentils in 180 ml water for 15 minutes until soft and the water is almost absorbed. Remove from the heat, stir in the bulgur and leave to swell, covered, for 20 minutes.
Finely dice the onion and sweat in the olive oil for 5 minutes until soft. Briefly toast the tomato and pepper paste, pul biber and cumin with it.
Knead the onion mixture, chopped spring onion, parsley, lemon juice and salt into the lentil and bulgur mixture.
With wet hands, shape into oblong patties, pressing them with your fingers.
Arrange on lettuce leaves, sprinkle with pomegranate seeds and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Githeri – Kenyan Corn and Bean Stew with Potatoes and Kale
instructions: Dice the onion and garlic and fry in the oil for 5 minutes until golden. Briefly toast the curry powder with them.
Dice the tomatoes, add them and cook for 5 minutes until they break down into a sauce.
Dice the potatoes and carrot, add with the corn, beans and stock and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Cut the kale into fine strips, fold in and cook for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt and serve sprinkled with coriander.

title: Green Spelt Patties with Creamed Savoy Cabbage and Potatoes
instructions: Bring the cracked green spelt to the boil in the stock and leave to swell, covered, for 15 minutes, then let it cool. Cook the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes.
Finely dice the onion and knead into the green spelt with the carrot, chickpea flour, mustard, marjoram, salt and pepper. Leave the mixture to rest for 10 minutes and shape into 3 patties.
Fry the patties in 7 g oil for 4 minutes per side until crisp.
Cut the savoy cabbage into fine strips, sweat in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, add the cooking cream, season with nutmeg and reduce for 3 minutes.
Serve the patties with the creamed savoy cabbage and parsley potatoes.

title: Harira – Moroccan Tomato Soup with Lentils, Chickpeas and Dates
ingredients: Ras el hanout, ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, lemon
instructions: Finely dice the onion and celery and sweat in the olive oil for 5 minutes. Briefly toast the spices and tomato purée with them.
Add the tomatoes, lentils and stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and vermicelli and cook for another 6 minutes.
Mix the flour with 4 tbsp water until smooth, pour it in while stirring and simmer the soup for 3 minutes until thickened. Stir in the chopped herbs.
Serve with lemon wedges and dates, as is customary during Ramadan.

title: Tempeh Tacos al Pastor with Pineapple and Red Cabbage
instructions: Soak the chillies in hot water for 10 minutes and purée finely with the orange juice, cumin, oregano, achiote and salt.
Cut the tempeh into thin strips, mix with the marinade and leave to infuse for 15 minutes.
Fry the tempeh in the oil for 6 minutes until the marinade caramelises. Cut the pineapple into small cubes and fry with it for the last 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Top with the tempeh, pineapple, diced onion, red cabbage and coriander and serve with lime.

title: Rajma Chawal – Punjabi Kidney Bean Curry with Rice and Cucumber Raita
ingredients: Cumin, garam masala, turmeric, chilli, coriander
instructions: Cook the basmati rice. Toast the cumin in the oil, finely dice the onion and fry for 8 minutes until golden brown.
Grate the ginger and garlic, add with the turmeric, chilli and garam masala and toast for 1 minute.
Purée the tomatoes, add them and reduce for 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the beans and 150 ml water, mash a few beans and simmer for 15 minutes until creamy.
Grate the cucumber, mix with the soy yoghurt, cumin and salt, and serve with the rajma, rice and coriander.

title: Thukpa – Tibetan Noodle Soup with Tofu and Vegetables
instructions: Dice the tofu, fry in the oil until browned all over and set aside.
Chop the onion, ginger and garlic and sweat for 3 minutes. Dice the tomato and cook for 2 minutes until it breaks down.
Add the stock and soy sauce, then the sliced carrot and shredded cabbage, and simmer for 8 minutes.
Cook the noodles separately, drain and place in a large bowl. Let the spinach and tofu warm through in the soup for 1 minute.
Ladle the soup over the noodles and sprinkle with spring onion and chilli.

title: Tofu Bhurji with Tomatoes, Peas, Spinach and Wholegrain Pav
ingredients: Green chilli, turmeric, cumin, kala namak (black salt), coriander
instructions: Toast the cumin in the oil, then fry the finely chopped onion, ginger and chilli for 3 minutes. Dice the tomato and cook for 2 minutes.
Roughly crumble the tofu with your fingers, add with the turmeric and peas and fry for 5 minutes.
Fold in the spinach and let it wilt. Season with kala namak and coriander.
Slice the rolls open and toast in a dry pan for 1 minute on each side.
Serve the bhurji with the warm pav, Mumbai-style, for filling or dipping.

title: Chickpea Omelette with Mushrooms, Spinach and Chives
ingredients: Kala namak (black salt), turmeric, baking powder, chives, pepper
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour with the water, nutritional yeast, turmeric, a pinch of baking powder and kala namak until smooth and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Dice the shallot, slice the mushrooms and fry in half of the oil for 5 minutes. Briefly wilt the spinach and set aside.
Heat the remaining oil in a non-stick pan, pour in the batter and let it set over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Place the mushroom and spinach filling on one half, fold the omelette over and fry for another 1 minute.
Sprinkle with chives and serve with toasted sourdough bread.

title: Natto Gohan with Miso Soup and Cucumber Tsukemono
instructions: Wash the rice and cook with 90 ml water for 15 minutes, then leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Thinly slice the cucumber, knead with a little salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out.
Heat 300 ml kombu dashi, dice the silken tofu and warm it in the dashi with the wakame. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the miso – do not let it boil again.
Stir the natto vigorously with the soy sauce until it forms strings and place on the rice.
Serve with spring onion, nori strips, the miso soup and the cucumber.

title: Fatteh – Lebanese Chickpeas with Pitta Chips and Tahini Soy Yoghurt
instructions: Tear the pitta into pieces and toast in the oven at 200°C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Heat the chickpeas with 50 ml water, cumin and salt for 5 minutes.
Stir the soy yoghurt with the tahini, grated garlic, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Toast the pine nuts in the olive oil until golden brown.
Place the pitta chips in a bowl, top with the warm chickpeas and a little of their liquid, pour over the tahini yoghurt and finish with the pine nuts, paprika, parsley and pomegranate.

title: Beans on Toast with Mushrooms and Spinach
instructions: Finely dice the onion and sweat in 2 g oil until translucent. Briefly toast the tomato purée with it.
Add the passata, maple syrup, smoked paprika and beans and simmer for 8 minutes until thick. Season to taste.
Quarter the mushrooms and fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until browned, add the spinach and let it wilt.
Toast the bread until golden brown.
Spoon the beans onto the toast and serve with the mushrooms and spinach.

title: Buckwheat Blini with Soy Yoghurt and Blueberries
instructions: Mix the linseeds with 2 tbsp water and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Mix the buckwheat flour, baking powder and salt, stir in the soy drink and linseeds and leave the batter to rest for 10 minutes.
Brush a pan with a little oil and add one tablespoon of batter per blini. Cook over medium heat for 1–2 minutes per side.
Make 8 small blini this way.
Serve with the soy yoghurt, blueberries and maple syrup.

title: Tapioca – Brazilian Cassava Crêpe with Banana, Peanut Butter and Cinnamon
instructions: Sift the tapioca flour evenly into a dry non-stick pan.
Cook over medium heat for 2 minutes until the starch sticks together into a flatbread, then turn and cook for another 1 minute.
Slice the banana, place on one half, drizzle with the peanut butter and dust with cinnamon.
Fold the crêpe over and serve with the soy yoghurt.

title: Akara – Nigerian Bean Fritters with Tomato-Pepper Sauce and Wholegrain Bread
instructions: Soak the black-eyed beans overnight, rub off the skins and purée with half of the onion, the chilli, salt and 3 tbsp water into a light batter. Beat vigorously for 3 minutes.
Fry tablespoons of the batter in 10 g hot oil in a pan for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Purée the tomatoes, pepper and remaining onion and cook down in the remaining oil for 10 minutes into a thick sauce.
Serve the akara hot with the sauce and wholegrain bread – Nigerian-style, ideally as a sandwich.

title: Molletes with Black Beans, Avocado and Pico de Gallo
instructions: Heat the black beans with the cumin, salt and 3 tbsp water and mash into a coarse purée.
Halve the rolls, spread with the bean purée, sprinkle with nutritional yeast and bake in the oven at 220°C for 6 minutes.
Finely dice the tomato, onion, jalapeño and coriander and mix with the lime juice and salt to make pico de gallo.
Top the molletes with the pico de gallo and avocado slices.

title: Amaranth Porridge with Mango, Coconut and Hemp Seeds
instructions: Rinse the amaranth in a fine sieve and bring to the boil with 100 ml water and half of the soy drink.
Simmer covered over low heat for 20 minutes until the grains are tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the remaining soy drink, the vanilla and maple syrup and stir for 2 minutes until creamy.
Dice the mango. Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the mango, desiccated coconut, hemp seeds and lime zest.

title: Spelt Banana Bread Muffins with Walnuts and Soy Yoghurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Mix the linseeds with 2 tbsp water and leave to swell.
Mash the banana and mix with the linseeds, maple syrup, soy drink and oil.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt, then stir in two thirds of the chopped walnuts.
Divide the batter between 2 muffin cases, sprinkle with the remaining walnuts and bake for 22 minutes.
Leave to cool slightly and serve with the soy yoghurt.

title: Tempeh TLT Sandwich with Tomato, Lettuce and Avocado
instructions: Cut the tempeh into very thin slices. Mix the soy sauce, maple syrup and smoked paprika.
Fry the tempeh in the oil for 2 minutes per side until crisp, deglaze with the marinade and glaze until it has evaporated.
Toast the bread and spread one slice with mashed avocado.
Top with lettuce, tomato slices and tempeh, cover with the second slice and cut in half diagonally.

title: Xian Doujiang – Taiwanese Savoury Soy Milk Soup with Flatbread
instructions: Finely dice the smoked tofu and slice the spring onion into rings.
Put the rice vinegar, soy sauce, tofu and half of the spring onion into a soup bowl.
Heat the soy drink until almost boiling and pour it briskly into the bowl. Wait briefly until the soy milk sets slightly and forms curds.
Top with the chilli sesame oil, white pepper and remaining spring onion.
Briefly toast the flatbread and serve alongside for dipping.

title: Tofu Benedict with Spinach and Cashew Hollandaise
ingredients: Turmeric, kala namak (black salt), lemon juice, chives
instructions: Soak the cashews for at least 2 hours, drain and blend with the soy drink, nutritional yeast, mustard, turmeric, lemon juice and kala namak into a smooth hollandaise. Warm gently.
Cut the tofu into two round slices 1.5 cm thick, season with turmeric and kala namak and fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side until golden yellow.
Wilt the spinach in the pan. Halve and toast the rolls, and slice the tomato.
Top the roll halves with tomato, spinach and tofu and coat with the hollandaise. Sprinkle with chives.

title: Bubur Kacang Hijau – Indonesian Mung Bean and Coconut Porridge with Banana
instructions: Soak the mung beans for 2 hours and drain.
Bring to the boil with 400 ml water, ginger slices and pandan and simmer for 30 minutes until the beans burst and turn creamy.
Stir in the sugar and a pinch of salt and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Briefly warm the coconut milk with a pinch of salt.
Spoon the porridge into bowls, pour over the coconut milk and top with banana slices and sesame seeds.

title: Muhammara – Syrian Red Pepper and Walnut Dip with Vegetable Sticks and Pitta
instructions: Roast the peppers at 230°C for 25 minutes until the skin blisters black, leave to cool covered and peel.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan. Coarsely purée with the peppers, breadcrumbs, pomegranate molasses, cumin, Aleppo pepper, lemon juice and salt.
Spread the dip into a bowl and drizzle with olive oil.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks, toast the pitta and cut into triangles, and serve both with the dip.

title: Cocoa Tahini Energy Balls with Dates and Sesame
instructions: Soak the dates in warm water for 10 minutes and drain well.
Process the dates with the tahini, oats, cocoa and salt in a mini chopper into a sticky mixture.
With wet hands, shape into 4 balls.
Roll in sesame seeds and chill for at least 30 minutes.

title: Funghi Ripieni – Stuffed Mushrooms with White Bean and Walnut Filling
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Twist the stalks out of the mushrooms and chop finely.
Fry the mushroom stalks and garlic in half of the oil for 3 minutes. Roughly mash the beans with a fork, chop the walnuts and parsley and mix everything with the lemon zest, oregano, salt and pepper.
Press the filling into the mushroom caps. Finely crumble the bread, mix with the remaining oil and sprinkle over the top.
Bake on a tray for 15–18 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the crumbs golden brown. Serve warm or lukewarm.

title: Pimientos de Padrón with Toasted Almonds, Lemon and Sea Salt
instructions: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 4 minutes and chop roughly.
Heat the olive oil in the pan until very hot and fry the peppers for 4–5 minutes until the skin blisters and darkens in places.
Immediately sprinkle with coarse sea salt and the almonds.
Serve with a lemon wedge and eat hot.

title: Elote – Grilled Corn on the Cob with Cashew-Lime Cream and Chilli
ingredients: Corn on the cob (pre-cooked, kernel weight)
instructions: Blend the cashews with 2 tbsp water, lime juice and salt into a smooth cream.
Brush the corn cobs with oil and grill on a barbecue or in a griddle pan for 8–10 minutes, turning, until charred in places.
Spread the hot cobs with the cashew cream.
Sprinkle with nutritional yeast, chilli powder and chopped coriander and serve with lime wedges.

title: Pkhali – Georgian Spinach and Walnut Balls with Pomegranate
ingredients: Utskho suneli (blue fenugreek), coriander seeds, salt
instructions: Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, refresh in cold water and squeeze out very thoroughly.
Grind the walnuts, garlic, spices and vinegar into a fine paste in a mini chopper.
Finely chop the spinach, coriander and onion, knead with the walnut paste and season with salt.
Shape into small balls, press a hollow into each with your thumb and fill with pomegranate seeds.
Serve with rye bread.

title: Matcha Latte with Soy Milk and Maple Syrup
instructions: Sift the matcha into a bowl and whisk with 50 ml hot but not boiling water (approx. 80°C) using a bamboo whisk until frothy.
Heat the soy drink and froth it.
Put the maple syrup into a large glass, pour in the matcha and top with the milk foam.

title: Strawberry Silken Tofu Smoothie with Oats
instructions: Wash and hull the strawberries, and break the banana into pieces.
Blend all the ingredients for 1 minute until very creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink immediately.

title: Soy Yoghurt with Pomegranate, Pistachios and Rose Water
instructions: Stir the soy yoghurt with a few drops of rose water and a pinch of cardamom until smooth.
Roughly chop the pistachios and finely dice the dates.
Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl and sprinkle with the pomegranate seeds, pistachios and dates.

title: Oven-Baked Kale Chips with Cashew and Nutritional Yeast Seasoning
ingredients: Smoked paprika, garlic powder, lemon juice, salt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 140°C (fan). Strip the kale from the stalks, tear into pieces, wash and spin very thoroughly dry.
Finely grind the cashews with the nutritional yeast, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Massage the kale with the olive oil and a little lemon juice and toss with the cashew seasoning.
Spread out on two lined baking trays and dry for 20–25 minutes until crisp, turning halfway through.

title: Puffed Quinoa Peanut Bars with Dark Chocolate
instructions: Finely chop the dates and stir with the peanut butter and maple syrup in a small pan over low heat until smooth.
Mix in the puffed quinoa, oats, chopped peanuts and salt.
Press the mixture firmly into a small lined tin and chill for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate, drizzle over the top, leave to set and cut into 2 bars.

title: Tteokbokki with Tofu, White Cabbage and Spring Onions
instructions: If the rice cakes are hard, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes.
Bring the stock to the boil with the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic in a wide pan.
Add the rice cakes, cubed tofu and chopped white cabbage and simmer for 8–10 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Add the spring onion in pieces, cook for 1 minute and serve sprinkled with sesame seeds.

title: Mango Coconut Pudding with Agar-Agar and Lime
instructions: Finely purée 120 g mango with the coconut milk and maple syrup.
Stir the agar-agar into 50 ml water, bring to the boil and boil vigorously for 2 minutes.
Stir in the mango purée, heat briefly and pour into a glass or ramekin. Chill for at least 1 hour until set.
Serve with the soy yoghurt, the remaining mango diced, lime zest and mint.

title: Seed Crackers with Cucumber, Tomato and Cress
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Mix the seeds, oats and salt with the water and leave to swell for 15 minutes.
Spread the mixture very thinly on a lined baking tray and cut into pieces after 10 minutes of baking.
Bake for another 35–40 minutes until the crackers are dry and crisp, then leave to cool.
Top with cucumber and tomato slices, cress, salt and pepper.

title: Chickpea Almond Cookies with Dark Chocolate
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Rinse the chickpeas well and pat dry.
Process with the almond butter, maple syrup, oats, baking powder, vanilla and salt in a mini chopper into a smooth dough.
Chop the chocolate and fold it in.
Shape 3 cookies, flatten on baking paper and bake for 14 minutes. Leave to firm up on the tray.
